subject: Archaeology
title: Great Zimbabwe's Stone Walls
description: One-minute skill: Great Zimbabwe's Stone Walls.

hook.text: In southern Africa, European explorers found massive stone walls and refused to believe Africans built them.

buildup.text: Great Zimbabwe was a wealthy trading city of 18,000 people, built between the 11th and 15th centuries.

discovery.text: Its walls are 36 feet tall and built without mortar — the stones fit together by precision alone.

twist.text: Colonial archaeologists invented theories about Phoenicians or lost white races to deny African achievement.

climax.text: Modern archaeology confirmed the Shona people built it. The country of Zimbabwe took its name from the site.

punchline.text: A nation named itself after the ruins racists refused to credit.

quiz.question: What false narrative did colonial archaeologists create about Great Zimbabwe?
options: They claimed it was a natural rock formation, not a human construction
They attributed it to Phoenicians or lost white races to deny African achievement
They said it was built by Arab traders who later abandoned the site

details.summary: Great Zimbabwe, built between the 11th and 15th centuries in southeastern Africa, features massive dry-stone walls up to 11 meters high constructed without mortar. It was the capital of a prosperous trading kingdom, but colonial-era Europeans refused to believe Africans built it.
details.whyItMatters: Great Zimbabwe's history is inseparable from racist denial. Colonial archaeologists attributed it to Phoenicians or Arabs rather than accept African achievement.
takeaways: Massive dry-stone walls built without mortar between 1100 and 1450 CE
Capital of a wealthy African trading kingdom
Colonial archaeologists denied African construction — now disproven

faq.question: Why did colonial-era scholars deny African builders?
faq.answer: Admitting that Africans built Great Zimbabwe contradicted the racist ideology that justified colonialism. Acknowledging advanced African civilization undermined the narrative that Europeans were civilizing a primitive continent.

faq.question: How did Great Zimbabwe become wealthy?
faq.answer: It controlled trade routes between inland gold and ivory sources and the Indian Ocean coast. Goods from China, Persia, and India have been found in the ruins. At its peak it housed 10,000-20,000 people and was the largest stone structure in sub-Saharan Africa south of Ethiopia.
